**SECTION B - COMPOSITION (40 marks)**

Mark distribution: Content and Organisation (12 marks); Expression (16 marks); Accuracy (12 marks).

Choose ONE topic to write on from the list below. You are advised to write clearly and effectively, to spell and punctuate correctly, and to ensure that your writing is appropriate in style and content to the topic chosen. Avoid obscene language and do not disclose your identity (name, school, parents, family background etc). You should write between 450 - 500 words.

questions.corrige_markdown:
**Plan**

1. Introduction: children as the future of the nation.
2. Their nature: playful, curious, innocent (descriptive angle).
3. Their needs: love, food, education, health, protection.
4. Dangers they face: child labour, abuse, street life.
5. Conclusion: our duty to care for them.

**Model composition (474 words)**

Children are the greatest gift that God gives to a family, and they are also the future of every nation. They are the leaders, doctors, teachers and farmers of tomorrow. For this reason, the way a society treats its children shows what kind of future it is preparing for itself.

By nature, children are playful, curious and innocent. Anybody who has watched them in a village courtyard on a sunny afternoon knows how full of life they are. They run after each other, laugh loudly, sing, and invent games with stones, sticks and old tyres. They ask endless questions about everything they see, because they want to understand the world. Their faces are bright, their eyes are full of hope, and they trust the adults who take care of them. When a child falls and hurts a knee, a kind word or a small hug is enough to bring back a smile. Such is the beauty of childhood, and it is a treasure which every adult should protect.

However, children cannot grow into useful citizens by themselves. They need love and affection first of all. A child who is loved at home develops confidence and learns to love others. Children also need good food, clean water and medical care to remain healthy, since they easily fall sick. Above all, they need education, which opens the door to a better life. School teaches them to read, to think and to behave well, and it prepares them for a profession.

Sadly, many children in our country and in the world do not enjoy these rights. Some are forced to work on farms or in markets when they should be in classrooms. Others are sent into the streets to sell goods or to beg, where they are exposed to accidents, bad company and violence. Some are beaten, insulted or abused by the very people who should protect them, and others are left without parents because of war, disease or poverty. These children grow up sad and sometimes become a danger to society.

It is therefore our duty, as parents, teachers, leaders and citizens, to protect and guide children. Parents should give them love, discipline and a good example. Teachers should be patient and fair. The government and organisations should build schools and hospitals, punish those who abuse children and support poor families. Even young people like us can help by being kind to younger ones and by sharing our knowledge with them.

In conclusion, children are like young plants. If we water them, protect them from storms and give them enough light, they will grow into strong trees that give shade and fruit to everybody. If we neglect them, they will wither and die, and our nation will lose its hope. Let us therefore care for our children today so that they may build a better tomorrow.

**Marking grid**

| Criterion | Marks | What earns the marks |
|---|---|---|
| Content and Organisation | 12 | Relevant ideas on children (nature, needs, dangers, our duty) developed with examples, in clear paragraphs with an introduction and a conclusion |
| Expression | 16 | Varied vocabulary and sentence structures, appropriate style and tone, fluent links between ideas |
| Accuracy | 12 | Correct grammar, tenses, spelling and punctuation |

**Common mistakes**

1. Writing only a definition or a list of points about children instead of a developed composition.
2. A composition with no introduction or conclusion and with paragraphs that jump from one idea to another.
